coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED (in priority order):
1. Wikipedia "2009 Alabama Crimson Tide football team" — has a real Coaching staff table (10 on-field coaches + Scott Cochran). Quotes taken from the RENDERED page text; in the rendered table the name and the position sit on separate lines, so the Wikipedia quotes I supply are the position cell text (the adjacent name is given in the note).
2. rolltide.com coaching-staff index page, Wayback capture of 2010-01-27 (20 days after the Jan. 7, 2010 BCS title game) — https://web.archive.org/web/20100127102344/http://www.rolltide.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/m-footbl-coaches.html . This is the single best "who was on staff at the championship" artifact: it lists exactly the same 10 on-field coaches plus Cochran, post-title-game. I verified by direct fetch that every quote I cite appears verbatim in that page.
3. Individual archived rolltide.com coach bio pages (same Jan. 2010 capture). Each page covers exactly one person, and the "Position:" field value is the quote. I fetched and string-verified all of them (Cochran's page 503'd on one retry but was fetched successfully earlier and his role is independently verified on the index page and in the media guide).
4. 2009 University of Alabama Football Media Guide PDF, archived: https://web.archive.org/web/20121112093719/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/alab/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/MediaGuide_09FB.pdf . Pages 99-103 carry extractable text (Cochran, Vollmar, Marynowitz, Conerly, Allen, Martin, Pruitt) — those quotes are real, copied from the PDF text layer and string-verified. Page 2 is the "2009 Alabama Football Directory" with extractable text.

WHAT IS IMAGE-ONLY (quote = ""): Media guide page 104 ("FOOTBALL SUPPORT") is a 6x5 grid of 30 headshot tiles with the name and title burned into each 95x136-pixel JPEG. There is NO text layer on that page (PDF text extraction returns 27 characters). I rendered and progressively zoomed the page and transcribed all 30 captions visually. Per instructions, those 30 rows carry quote:"" with the transcribed caption in the note. Transcriptions are high-confidence except where flagged.

KNOWN TRANSCRIPTION LIMIT: Troy Finney's caption's first line reads "SENIOR DIRECTOR"; the second line is below the raster's resolution limit and I could not read it. It is most likely "VIDEO OPERATIONS" (a general web search surfaced a Troy Finney / Alabama football "Director of Video Operations" association, but not from a citable contemporaneous source), so I left the role as the legible portion only rather than guess. Do not treat the bracketed part as sourced.

TIERS I COULD NOT RECOVER:
- ANALYSTS: Alabama published no "analyst" tier in 2009. The people who would later be called analysts appear here under graduate-assistant or support titles. Notably Joe Judge is listed in the 2009 media guide as "Video Graduate Assistant," while later national coverage (and Wikipedia) describe his 2009-2011 Alabama role as "special teams assistant" / "football analyst." I recorded his 2009 title as the school worded it and cited the Wikipedia/Judge page as corroboration that he was on the 2009 staff. If your ring rule wants an "analyst" bucket for 2009 Alabama, it is empty by the school's own labeling.
- QUALITY CONTROL: no one at Alabama carried a "quality control" title in any 2009 document I found. The qc bucket is empty, not unrecovered-but-existing.
- STUDENT MANAGERS / TRAINING-STAFF INTERNS / additional S&C interns beyond the five named: not published anywhere I could locate. Alabama listed one S&C student assistant (Sedrick Irvin) by name; there were certainly more unnamed student assistants and equipment/managerial students who are undocumented.
- MID-SEASON CHANGES: I found no documented arrival or departure between the Sept. 5, 2009 opener and the Jan. 7, 2010 title game. The staff changes Wikipedia documents (Kevin Steele to Clemson, Lance Thompson to Tennessee, both January 2009; Sunseri and Willis hired later that month) are all pre-season, so Steele and Thompson are correctly EXCLUDED — they were not on the 2009 staff. No midseason_note is set on anyone.
- SNAPSHOT-DATE CAVEAT: the 30-person support grid comes from the preseason (August 2009) media guide. The Jan. 27, 2010 rolltide.com capture confirms the 11 coaching/S&C-head names post-championship, but I could NOT find a January-2010 equivalent listing for the support tier. The 2010 BCS bowl guide PDF is indexed in the Wayback CDX (2010-bcs-bowl-guide) but every retrieval path I tried returned an HTML error page rather than the PDF, so support-staff membership is verified as of August 2009, not as of the title game.

SCOPE NOTE: The media guide's own "Football Support" section includes athletics-department people attached to football (media relations, creative media, academic advisors, FCA director, two state troopers). I included them all with role_category "other" rather than silently pruning, so you can decide where your ring rule draws the line. Total: 47 documented people (1 head coach, 9 on-field assistants, 7 strength & conditioning, 5 graduate assistants, 10 operations/personnel/administrative, 5 medical, 2 equipment, 8 other). Nobody in this list is inferred — every row traces to a named source.
